title: Chromosome 6q mediated loss of LATS1 tumour suppression as a targetable mechanism of ultra-high-risk posterior fossa A ependymoma
title_zh: 6q染色体介导的LATS1肿瘤抑制失活：一种可靶向的极高危后枕区A型脊髓膜瘤机制
abstract: Abstract Posterior Fossa A (PFA) is the most frequent and clinically aggressive ependymoma (EPN) subgroup, with relapse typically representing a terminal event despite intensive multimodal therapy. Ultra-high-risk PFA EPNs are characterised by chromosome 6q loss (6q-) with or without chromosome 1q gain (1q +). While the molecular mechanisms driving 1q+ have been elucidated, 6q- PFA pathobiology remains poorly understood. Here, we show that loss of 6q in PFA EPN results in deletion of LATS1 (Large Tumour Suppressor Kinase 1), thereby dysregulating the Hippo signalling pathway and enhancing YAP/TEAD activity. Integrated analyses of primary and recurrent PFA EPNs, incorporating clinical, multiomic, and functional assays, were performed to define the biology and therapeutic susceptibility of 6q- PFA EPNs. Cumulative 6q loss was associated with nearly half of PFA EPN-related deaths. Copy number profiling identified the LATS1 locus as recurrently deleted across all 6q- cases, including 10/60 with partial 6q deletions. Restoration of LATS1 expression in 6q- PFA cell lines re-established protein levels and suppressed proliferation. Tumour analyses showed marked Hippo pathway disruption with elevated YAP expression and TEAD2- related transcriptional activity. TEAD2 palmitoylation inhibitor VT107, and Proteolysis Targeted Chimera (PROTAC) degrader H122, exhibited PFA 6q- selective activity in vitro. TEAD2 upregulation was further observed in a previously described undifferentiated, progenitor-like population of PFA EPN cells. In conclusion, 6q loss defines an aggressive biological subset of PFA associated with dismal outcomes. Identification of LATS1 as a recurrently lost tumour suppressor implicates Hippo pathway dysregulation as a central driver of malignancy, and we identify YAP/TEAD signalling as a potential therapeutic target.
abstract_zh: 摘要：后枕区A型（PFA）脊髓膜瘤是最常见且临床上最具侵袭性的亚组，复发往往是终末事件，尽管接受强力多模态治疗。极高危PFA脊髓膜瘤的特征是6q染色体缺失（6q-），可伴随1q染色体增益（1q+）。虽然已阐明1q+的分子机制，但6q- PFA的病理生理仍不清楚。本研究显示，PFA脊髓膜瘤中6q缺失导致LATS1（大型肿瘤抑制激酶1）基因缺失，从而破坏Hippo信号通路并增强YAP/TEAD活性。我们对原发和复发PFA脊髓膜瘤进行整合分析，结合临床、多组学和功能实验，阐明了6q- PFA脊髓膜瘤的生物学特征和治疗敏感性。累计6q缺失与近一半PFA脊髓膜瘤相关死亡相关。拷贝数分析发现LATS1位点在所有6q-病例中反复缺失，包括10/60例部分6q缺失。恢复6q- PFA细胞系中LATS1表达可恢复蛋白水平并抑制增殖。肿瘤分析显示Hippo通路显著失调，YAP表达升高，TEAD2相关转录活性增强。TEAD2棕榈酰化抑制剂VT107和PROTAC降解剂H122在体外对PFA 6q-显示选择性活性。TEAD2上调亦在先前描述的未分化、祖细胞样PFA脊髓膜瘤细胞群中观察到。综上，6q缺失定义了一个与不良预后相关的侵袭性PFA亚群。识别LATS1为反复缺失的肿瘤抑制因子，提示Hippo通路失调是恶性进展的核心驱动因素，我们将YAP/TEAD信号作为潜在治疗靶点。
